'''Andrius Kubilius'''{{efn|{{IPA|lt|ˈɐnʲdʲrʲʊs kʊˈbɪlʲʊs}}}} (born 8 December 1956) is a [[Lithuania]]n politician who is currently serving as the [[European Commissioner]] for Defence and Space in the [[Second von der Leyen Commission]]. He previously served as a [[Member of the European Parliament]] (MEP) from 2019 to 2024 and as [[Prime Minister of Lithuania]] from 1999 to 2000 and again from 2008 to 2012.<ref name=VRK>LR Vyriausioji rinkimų komisija. [http://www.vrk.lt/rinkimai/400_lt/Kandidatai/Kandidatas19520/Kandidato19520Biografija.html Lietuvos Respublikos Seimo rinkimai] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081015043112/http://www.vrk.lt/rinkimai/400_lt/Kandidatai/Kandidatas19520/Kandidato19520Biografija.html |date=15 October 2008 }}. Retrieved on 24 November 2008</ref> He was the leader of the conservative political party [[Homeland Union]] from 2003 to 2015, of which he continues to be a member.

==Early life and education==
Kubilius was born in [[Vilnius]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://andriuskubilius.lt/en/about/ |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=Andrius Kubilius |language=en-US}}</ref> After graduation from the 22nd secondary school in Vilnius, Kubilius was accepted to [[Vilnius University]] and studied in the Faculty of Physics until 1979. He continued his academic career and postgraduate studies at Vilnius University from 1981 to 1984.<ref>Gary Peach (8 September 2010), [https://www.politico.eu/article/history-buff/ History buff] ''[[European Voice]]''.</ref>

==Career in Lithuanian politics==
===Early career ===
[[File:Flickr - europeanpeoplesparty - EPP Congress Warsaw (396).jpg|thumb|Kubilius with Polish Prime Minister [[Donald Tusk]] in Warsaw, 29 April 2009]]
Kubilius became a member of the pro-independence ''[[Sąjūdis]]'' movement, who favoured independence from the occupation of the Soviet Union. He later became the Executive Secretary of the Sąjūdis Council. Soon after the re-establishment of [[Act of the Re-Establishment of the State of Lithuania|Lithuania's independence]], Kubilius was elected to the [[Seimas]] (parliament). Since then Kubilius has been an active figure in Lithuanian politics. He became a member of the Homeland Union – Lithuanian Christian Democrats in 1993.<ref name=VRK/>

Between 1996 and 1999 Kubilius served as Deputy Speaker of Seimas.

=== 10th Prime Minister of Lithuania, 1999–2000 ===
After [[Rolandas Paksas]] resigned as the Prime Minister of Lithuania, Kubilius became prime minister forming the [[Kubilius Cabinet I|first Kubilius cabinet]] and serving until the [[2000 Lithuanian parliamentary election|2000 parliamentary election]].

In 2000, he supported a law passed on 13 June by the Seimas seeking compensation from Russia for damages inflicted during the [[Soviet occupation of Lithuania|illegal Soviet occupation of Lithuania and the Baltics]], a key issue for the prime minister and Homeland Union.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=COMPENSATION ISSUE RETURNS TO POLITICAL AGENDA. |url=https://jamestown.org/program/compensation-issue-returns-to-political-agenda/ |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=jamestown.org |language=en-US}}</ref> The move was endorsed by Estonian Prime Minister [[Mart Laar]] and Latvian Prime Minister [[Andris Bērziņš (Latvian Prime Minister)|Andris Berzins]], who both supported cooperation in the [[Baltic Assembly]] on the issue.<ref name=":3" />

=== 14th Prime Minister of Lithuania, 2008–2012 ===
Kubilius led the Homeland Union – Lithuanian Christian Democrats Party into elections on 28 October 2008. His Homeland Union won the election representing a victory for Lithuania's center right after seven years of leftist rule.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2008-10-13 |title=Conservatives gain in Lithuania voting (Published 2008) |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/10/13/world/europe/13iht-lithuania.4.16911788.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230122131619/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/10/13/world/europe/13iht-lithuania.4.16911788.html |archive-date=2023-01-22 |access-date=2024-12-31 |language=en}}</ref> Kubilius was already known as a sharp critic of the Russian regime; Homeland Union promised to combat dependence on Russian energy and enact needed economic reforms.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2008-10-28 |title=Lithuania installs conservative party critical of Russia - Taipei Times |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/world/archives/2008/10/28/2003427175 |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=Taipei Times |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Following the election Kubilius was, as expected, nominated as the Homeland Union's candidate for Prime Minister. The coalition agreement was signed on 17 November.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pasirašyta Permainų koalicijos sutartis |url=https://www.delfi.lt/news/daily/lithuania/pasirasyta-permainu-koalicijos-sutartis-19302657 |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=Delfi |language=lt}}</ref> On 27 November 2008 Kubilius was officially appointed as Prime Minister of Lithuania forming the [[Kubilius Cabinet II|second Kubilius cabinet]]. The cabinet received 89 votes in favour, 27 against, and 16 abstentions in the confidence vote in the [[Seimas]].

After taking office, he "cut public spending by 30%, slashed pensions by 11% and even took a pay cut of 45% himself".<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |title=Leftward lurch |url=https://www.economist.com/europe/2012/11/03/leftward-lurch |access-date=2024-12-31 |work=The Economist |issn=0013-0613}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/04/02/business/global/02austerity.html|title = From Lithuania, a View of Austerity's Costs|newspaper = The New York Times|date = 2 April 2010|last1 = Thomas|first1 = Landon Jr.}}</ref> He followed a policy of diversifying Lithuania's energy supplies away from Russia including filing a lawsuit against [[Gazprom]], then Lithuania's sole supplier of natural gas, seeking over €1 billion in damages and depriving the Russian company of control over Lithuanian infrastructure.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SKNVibes {{!}} Lithuania sues Russia's Gazprom over pricing |url=https://www.sknvibes.com/news/newsdetails.cfm/64110 |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=www.sknvibes.com |agency=AFP}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-12-19 |title=The centre-left government takes power in Lithuania |url=https://www.osw.waw.pl/en/publikacje/analyses/2012-12-19/centre-left-government-takes-power-lithuania |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=OSW Centre for Eastern Studies |language=en}}</ref> He was active in seeking financial compensation from Russia for the [[Occupation of Lithuania by Soviet Union 1940|illegal Soviet occupation of Lithuania]], labeling the issue a priority upon taking office in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lithuania demands compensation from Russia |url=https://en.apa.az/cis-countries/-93264 |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=Apa.az |language=en}}</ref> In 2011, the issue continued to be a priority with his foreign minister labeling it "ridiculous to talk with Russia without resolving issues related to the occupation."<ref>{{Cite web |last=BNN |date=2011-10-19 |title=Lithuania still hopes to receive compensation from Russia |url=https://bnn-news.com/lithuania-hopes-receive-compensation-russia-39203 |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=Baltic News Network |language=en-US}}</ref> He instituted a commission on 23 May 2012 to move the issue forward.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2012-05-30 |title=The Lithuanian government is resuming the topic of claims linked to Soviet occupation ahead of the election |url=https://www.osw.waw.pl/en/publikacje/analyses/2012-05-30/lithuanian-government-resuming-topic-claims-linked-to-soviet |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=OSW Centre for Eastern Studies |language=en}}</ref> He also called for the issue of financial compensation from Russia to be included as a condition of EU-Russia relations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lithuanian Prime Minister thinks Soviet occupation compensation should be included in EU-Russian dialogue |url=https://www.15min.lt/en/article/opinion/lithuanian-prime-minister-thinks-soviet-occupation-compensation-should-be-included-in-eu-russian-dialogue-530-234545 |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=en.15min.lt |language=en}}</ref> His strong stance towards the Russian regime resulted in a freeze of relations between Lithuania and Moscow.<ref name=":4" />

As a result of his policies, Lithuania made one of strongest economic recoveries in Europe.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://euobserver.com/opinion/114419|title = &#91;Opinion&#93; Lithuania's remarkable recovery| date=28 November 2011 }}</ref> Kubilius is considered by some as being the best Prime Minister in Lithuania's modern history.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tspmi.vu.lt/komentarai/k-girnius-kubiliaus-ir-sveiko-proto-pergale/|title = K. Girnius. Kubiliaus ir sveiko proto pergalė|newspaper = Tspmi}}</ref> Among his accomplishments were reining in public expenditures, preparation to join the [[Eurozone]], and reform of the energy sector.<ref name=":2" /> However, his Homeland Union party lost the 2012 election to succeed him leading to the [[Butkevičius Cabinet]]. Kubilius became the first prime minister of Lithuania to serve his entire term.<ref>[[Lietuvos rytas]] [http://lietuvosdiena.lrytas.lt/-12277782251226792187-a-kubilius-%C4%AF-premjerus-u%C5%BEtikrinta-persvara-video-papildyta-15-val-27-min.htm A.Kubilius į premjerus – užtikrinta persvara] Retrieved on 13 October 2016</ref> According to ''[[The Economist]]'', "the election came too early for Mr. Kubilius to benefit from a recovery from the painful austerity measures that he imposed when he realised that Lithuania risked becoming the Baltic Greece."<ref name=":2" /> He was viewed as having "sacrificed his political popularity" to save the country from bankruptcy following leftist rule.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Lithuania's final sprint |url=https://www.economist.com/eastern-approaches/2012/09/07/lithuanias-final-sprint |access-date=2024-12-31 |work=The Economist |issn=0013-0613}}</ref>

== European Union career ==

===Member of the European Parliament, 2019–2024===
In 2019, Kubilius was [[2019 European Parliament election in Lithuania|elected]] a [[Member of the European Parliament]] for [[Homeland Union]] and served as a member of the [[European People's Party Group]]. He served on the [[European Parliament Committee on Foreign Affairs|Committee on Foreign Affairs]] and the [[Committee on Industry, Research and Energy]].<ref name="Andrius Kubilius">[https://www.europarl.europa.eu/meps/en/197843/ANDRIUS_KUBILIUS/home Andrius Kubilius] [[European Parliament]].</ref>

In addition to his committee assignments, Kubilius was part of the parliament's delegations to the [[Euronest Parliamentary Assembly]] and to the EU-Ukraine Parliamentary Association Committee.<ref name="Andrius Kubilius" /> He was also a member of the [[Spinelli Group]].<ref>[https://thespinelligroup.eu/board-members/ Board & Members] [[Spinelli Group]].</ref>

In November 2021, Kubilius joined a group of seven Members of the European Parliament led by [[Raphaël Glucksmann]] to [[Taiwan]] to send a strong signal in support of the self-ruling island, despite a threat of retaliation from China.<ref>Sarah Anne Aarup and Stuart Lau (2 November 2021), [https://www.politico.eu/article/meps-set-to-land-in-taiwan-on-tuesday-defying-beijing/ MEPs set to land in Taiwan on Tuesday, defying Beijing] ''[[Politico Europe]]''.</ref>

==== Standing rapporteur on Russia ====
In 2020, he was appointed the parliament's standing [[rapporteur]] on [[Russia–European Union relations|relations with Russia]].<ref>Hans von der Burchard (8 February 2021), [https://www.politico.eu/article/ursula-von-der-leyen-backs-josep-borrell-amid-calls-for-resignation-humiliating-russia-trip/ Von der Leyen backs Borrell amid calls for resignation over ‘humiliating’ Russia trip] ''[[Politico Europe]]''.</ref> In this role, he was responsible for forming the European Parliament's position on the subject matter.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Andrius Kubilius appointed European Parliament's Standing Rapporteur on Russia |url=https://www.15min.lt/en/article/politics/andrius-kubilius-appointed-european-parliament-s-standing-rapporteur-on-russia-526-1370346 |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=en.15min.lt |language=en}}</ref> Accepting the role, Kubilius stated, "My critical view of the Kremlin regime was formed long ago, and it is unchanging. I have made no effort to conceal it while at the European Parliament.”<ref name=":1" />

In 2021, he stated it is "impossible" to have good relations with Russia and called for the EU to phase out its [[Russia in the European energy sector|imports of oil and natural gas from Russia]].<ref>{{cite news |date=16 September 2021 |title=EU Parliament touts Russia oil, gas import phase-out |url=https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news/2254544-eu-parliament-touts-russia-oil-gas-import-phaseout |work=Argus Media}}</ref> He praised [[Turkey]] for "proving thrice [in Syria, Libya and Nagorno-Karabakh] that the Kremlin fears the fist."<ref>{{cite news |date=13 November 2020 |title=A. Kubilius. The Karabakh Knot: who is stronger – Turkey or Russia? |url=https://www.15min.lt/en/article/politics/a-kubilius-the-karabakh-knot-who-is-stronger-turkey-or-russia-526-1407422 |work=[[15min]]}}</ref> On the 12th anniversary of the [[Russian invasion of Georgia]] in 2020, Kubilius noted Russia's "continued provocations" in Georgia stating that they "grossly violate international law".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrius Kubilius – The only one European way for Russia is to take an example from Georgia, a role model for successful European reforms |url=https://1tv.ge/lang/en/news/andrius-kubilius-creeping-annexation-grossly-violates-international-law/ |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=1TV |language=en-US}}</ref> He led the call by the [[European People's Party]] for sanctions against all those responsible for Russia's [[poisoning of Alexei Navalny]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sanction Russian officials involved in Navalny poisoning and end Nord Stream 2 |url=https://www.eppgroup.eu/newsroom/sanction-russian-officials-involved-in-navalny-poisoning |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=www.eppgroup.eu |language=en}}</ref>

===European Commission, 2024–present===

In July 2024, Kubilius was nominated by the Lithuanian government to be his country's EU commissioner. Lithuanian President [[Gitanas Nausėda]] gave his approval on 22 August.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-22 |title=Lithuanian president approves Kubilius as candidate for European Commission |url=https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/2344943/lithuanian-president-approves-kubilius-as-candidate-for-european-commission |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=lrt.lt |language=en}}</ref> His nomination was approved by the [[Seimas]] in 3 September with Kubilius eyeing portfolios related to defence, security, and EU enlargement as ideal for Lithuania given Europe's security crisis.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-03 |title=Lithuanian parliament approves Kubilius as candidate for European Commission |url=https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/2352189/lithuanian-parliament-approves-kubilius-as-candidate-for-european-commission |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=lrt.lt |language=en}}</ref>

In September, [[Ursula von der Leyen|President von der Leyen]] allocated the Defence and Space portfolio to Kubilius.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lithuania's Andrius Kubilius named defense and space commissioner |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/lithuanias-andrius-kubilius-named-defense-and-space-commissioner/ |access-date=6 November 2024 |agency=Politico}}</ref> He is the first to hold the post.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-11-06 |title=5 things to know about defense chief Andrius Kubilius' European Parliament hearing |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/andrius-kubilius-defense-space-chief-european-parliament-hearing-russia/ |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=POLITICO |language=en-GB}}</ref> The creation of the post indicated that security had become a key item on the EU's agenda.<ref name="Reuters">{{Cite news |title=New EU defence chief to fight political battles with military edge |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/new-eu-defence-chief-fight-political-battles-with-military-edge-2024-09-17/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207013634/https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/new-eu-defence-chief-fight-political-battles-with-military-edge-2024-09-17/ |archive-date=2024-12-07 |access-date=2024-12-30 |work=Reuters |language=en-US}}</ref> His nomination was approved by the European Parliament on 7 November allowing him to take the office.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-05 |title=Lithuania's commissioner hearing: Andrius Kubilius bids to become EU's first defense boss — live updates |url=https://www.politico.eu/article/european-commissioner-hearings-lithuania-andrius-kubilius-defense-space/#id_1307634 |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=POLITICO |language=en-GB}}</ref> Upon taking office he stated that his priority would be strengthening the bloc's defence military deterrence capabilities.<ref name=":0" />

==Personal life==
Kubilius is married to Rasa Kubilienė, a violinist in the [[Lithuanian National Symphony Orchestra]]; the couple have two sons: Andrius Kubilius and Vytautas Kubilius, and three grandchildren.<ref>Gary Peach (8 September 2010), [https://www.politico.eu/article/history-buff/ History buff] ''[[European Voice]]''.</ref> In addition to his native [[Lithuanian language|Lithuanian]], Kubilius also speaks English and Russian.<ref name="VRK"/>
